newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt says tariff policy timing crucial.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt says tariff policy timing crucial.

text.p: The timing of South Africa's tariff policy was crucial in helping the government meet its job creation targets, officials said on Tuesday.

"The challenge is to find a way of creating 403,000 jobs annually by the year 2000...in terms of this the timing of tariff policy is of the essence," said Zav Rustomjee, director-general of the Department of Trade and Industry.

Addressing a public hearing on trade and industry policy in Pretoria he said if government did not place pressure on industries to transform, the gap between South African and successful international industries would continue to widen and lead to loss of employment.

The textile, clothing and motor industries had so far seen accelerated restructuring and a degree of employment loss but "had emerged relatively robust and able to face international competition," Rustomjee said.

He said the focus had to be on raising competitiveness. Difficulties included the fact that many industries still operated in "rand-seeking mode" and some of them had "missed the boat" while others did not know how to face new competitiveness.
The weakness of customs and excise was hampering competitiveness and had to be strengthened if tariff policy was to be more effective.
Rustomejee noted that the reduction in tariffs had been less steep than was often claimed. A number of support measures to cushion the impact of tariff reduction were already in place.
These included cluster studies and the coordination of sector strategy.
"A whole lot of support measures have already been put in place. But we can only do so much. Each of the social partners has a responsibility in those areas," he said.
